signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags JPY as the weekly leader at +0.578% average gain across 7 pairs, while AUD sits as the laggard at −0.672% across 4 pairs, creating a 1.250% bilateral spread. Despite this price momentum, AUD/JPY retains a massive +362bp OIS carry advantage (RBA AONIA 4.85% vs BoJ TONA 1.23%). AUD/USD trades below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6750, while USD/JPY holds above its moving averages at 159.61. The 1.250% spread reflects active cross-asset de-risking as equity markets pull back, forcing severe compression on high-beta carry pairs regardless of the underlying interest rate buffer. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY, momentum and equity-led risk reduction overriding carry support. Catalyst: Australia Wage Price Index release on 17 Nov at 00:30 UTC. Risk: VIX declines below 20 and equity markets rebound, re-establishing carry dominance.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium vs Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.61, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.22/157.42/158.67. A 267bp OIS carry differential (Fed SOFR 3.90% vs BoJ TONA 1.23%) continues to support the dollar, but options markets show clear caution. The 1M 25d Risk Reversal sits at −1.74, indicating significant put skew as institutional market participants actively pay up for downside protection. CFTC data shows JPY Leveraged Funds net short at −21,213 contracts, placing positioning at the 92nd percentile of its 52-week range (z=+1.46σ). The combination of a crowded carry trade and elevated put demand highlights asymmetric downside risk if verbal intervention escalates near the key 160.00 psychological threshold. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while holding above 158.22 SMA20. Catalyst: US Retail Sales release on 17 Nov at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Break below 158.22 SMA20 or sustained spot action above 160.00 triggering official MoF/BoJ FX intervention.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5508, remaining below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5629/0.5665/0.5814. Leveraged Funds hold a net short of −23,350 contracts (pctl 21), reflecting persistent institutional bearishness. This positioning aligns with New Zealand's Economic Surprise Index of −28.4, which marks the weakest data trajectory in the G10 following continuous macro misses. However, retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data is positioned 93% long, creating an extreme institutional vs. retail divergence. When retail long positioning reaches such extreme levels while macroeconomic data severely disappoints, the risk of retail capitulation accelerates downside momentum toward lower support. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, macro data weakness and retail extreme confirming downtrend. Catalyst: RBNZ Governor Orr Speech on 16 Nov at 22:00 UTC. Risk: Hawkish shift in RBNZ commentary triggering a short-covering rally above the 0.5629 SMA20.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Yield Spread vs Technical Structure
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3185, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3361/1.3341/1.3415, with the 20-day moving average sloping downward. The UK 2Y yield spread vs US 2Y expanded by +12bp over 5D to +25bp, while 2-year gilt yields breached 5.00% following hawkish Bank of England rate expectations. despite the underlying rate support, price action remains contained under technical resistance. The 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 6.2% against realized HV30 at 5.6%, reflecting a minor +0.6% vol risk premium. Yield momentum favors Cable resilience, but clear technical rejection below the 1.3361 SMA20 keeps broad price action range-bound. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, short-term rate support offset by technical resistance. Catalyst: UK CPI release on 18 Nov at 07:00 UTC. Risk: UK CPI print above 2.7% forecast forcing a bullish breakout through the 1.3361 SMA20.
